title.narrative: Provision of integrated agriculture and protection services for improved food security in Shaq Al Nile Khartoum

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International (RI), in partnership with Auttach for Peace and Development (APD), is implementing a comprehensive humanitarian intervention to address acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 4) and protection risks in Sharg Al Nile, Khartoum, targeting 14,190 of the most vulnerable individuals, including displaced populations, women and girls at high risk of gender-based violence (GBV), persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups. The deteriorating humanitarian situation has exacerbated protection concerns, including GBV during agricultural activities and aid distributions, exclusion of vulnerable groups from assistance, and conflicts over scarce resources such as arable land between farmers and nomadic communities. Additionally, widespread displacement has disrupted livelihoods, forcing families to adopt harmful coping strategies like child labor and early marriage, while poorly managed distribution points and unsafe transit routes further expose women and children to exploitation and violence. To strengthen food security and livelihoods, RI will distribute improved vegetable seeds, agricultural tools, egg-laying chickens with feed and housing materials, and fish farming kits, accompanied by training on climate-smart agriculture, poultry and fish production, nutrition-sensitive farming techniques, and income-generating activities (IGAs) such as food processing and tailoring. These interventions are informed by market assessments and community consultations to ensure cultural appropriateness, sustainability, and alignment with local economic opportunities. Recognizing the critical need for protection services, RI will establish a Women and Girls Safe Space (WGSS) to provide a secure environment for vulnerable women and girls, offering case management, psychosocial support, dignity kits for menstrual hygiene management, and referrals to specialized services. GBV safety audits will be conducted to identify and mitigate risks, while community-based protection networks will enhance local capacity to monitor threats and facilitate access to essential services through sensitization sessions and strengthened referral pathways. ltbrgt ltbrgtComplementing these efforts, RI’s Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items (ESNFI) response will deliver life-saving assistance to 440 households in Sharg Al Nile, in line with Sudan’s 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP). Distributed items—including tarpaulins, blankets, sleeping mats, cooking utensils, solar lamps, and jerry cans—will address immediate shelter needs and reduce exposure to harsh environmental conditions. The project’s Theory of Change is grounded in the integration of food security, protection, and NFI interventions: by equipping communities with productive assets, skills training, and safety nets, the project aims to improve food security, reduce protection risks, and enhance resilience to ongoing shocks, ultimately fostering long-term stability. Targeting and verification will adhere to FSL and Protection Cluster guidelines, with a strong emphasis on inclusivity and accountability. RI will implement robust monitoring and evaluation systems, including post-distribution monitoring, beneficiary feedback mechanisms, and satisfaction surveys, to ensure transparency, adapt programming to evolving needs, and measure impact. By addressing the interconnected challenges of food insecurity, inadequate shelter, and protection risks, this multi-sectoral response seeks to safeguard the dignity and well-being of crisis-affected communities in Khartoum while laying the foundation for sustainable recovery. ltbrgtlt/pgt
